title: The gated panel's 12px class sentence is set at 4.76:1, under the room's AAA rule
evidence:
examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:50-52 ("ink, ink-2, ink-3 carry text at or under 15px, including the 12px --bd-label, so they take AAA")
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level2/l2-dossier-3.css:52 `.bd-class { font-size: var(--bd-label) }`, :83 `.bd-zone[data-class="GATED"] .bd-class[data-class="GATED"] { color: var(--bd-gate-ink-2) }`
$ node design/check-contrast.mjs
  ok     --bd-gate-ink-2 #8a5c52     4.76:1 on gated sheet 2/2    floor 4.5   the panel's labels and class sentence (AAA owed)
body:
## Summary
`--bd-gate-ink-2` carries the inverted gated panel's 12px class sentence and labels at 4.76:1 on the sheet's darker stop; check-contrast.mjs's own rule gives 12px text AAA (7:1).

## Description
examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:50-52 sets AAA for every ink that carries text at or under 15px, "including the 12px --bd-label". In the gated zone, examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level2/l2-dossier-3.css:83 and :150 set `.bd-class` (font-size `--bd-label`, l2-dossier-3.css:52) and `.bd-block-label` in `--bd-gate-ink-2` (#8a5c52, components/board/style/base/tokens.css:137) on `--bd-gate-sheet` (tokens.css:131, stops #fbf4f2 / #f4eae7). Measured this round (check-contrast now models the panel, f832bf4): 4.76:1 on the foot stop, 5.18:1 on the top. That passes AA, so the instrument floors it at 4.5 with 'AAA owed' in its role. The text it fails on is the sentence that says an act reaches a person and cannot be undone. Fixed: retune --bd-gate-ink-2 darker (about #5e3a33 reaches 7:1 on #f4eae7) and raise its floor to 7.0. Out of this round's paths: tokens.css belongs to hirelane-board-ui.

## Flow
- open a candidate's dossier -> the GATED zone of the action bar renders `.bd-class` ("reaches the person" class sentence) at 12px in --bd-gate-ink-2 on the light sheet
- node design/check-contrast.mjs -> `ok --bd-gate-ink-2 #8a5c52 4.76:1 on gated sheet 2/2 floor 4.5`
- fix: in check-contrast.mjs set the floor to 7.0 (seed: goes red), retune tokens.css's --bd-gate-ink-2 until green, check the greyscale test (§7.1) still holds

## Expected impact
A reader deciding on an irreversible act reads its class sentence at AAA, like every other 12px label in the room; measured by check-contrast's printed ratio. Could break: the panel's label hierarchy if the darker ink flattens gate-ink against gate-ink-2 (15.34:1); keep them a legible step apart.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the gated panel's smallest text meets the AAA floor the rest of the room's small text meets
Before: 4.76:1 (--bd-gate-ink-2 on #f4eae7), measured by check-contrast.mjs after f832bf4
After: >= 7.0:1 predicted for a retune near #5e3a33 (computed, not built)
Method: probe - the ratio is computed by the shipped checker; the retune is out of this round's write set (tokens.css) and the visual result needs a browser
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The foot's register disclosure has neither of the app's two focus rings
evidence:
examples/hirelane/app/globals.css:57 :where(a, button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/base/the-room.css:87 .bd-root :where(button, select, textarea, input, a, [tabindex]):focus-visible
examples/hirelane/components/board/shell/Foot.tsx:86 <details className="bd-register">  :87 <summary>
$ grep -rn "summary" components/board/style -> the-foot.css only (no :focus-visible)
body:
## Summary
Both focus-visible rules - app/globals.css and the board's the-room.css - list button, a, input, select, textarea and [tabindex] but not `summary`, so the foot's capability disclosure is the one control that falls back to the browser's own ring.

## Description
examples/hirelane/app/globals.css:57 `:where(a, button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible` (2px, offset 2px, --dk-accent) and examples/hirelane/components/board/style/base/the-room.css:87 `.bd-root :where(button, select, textarea, input, a, [tabindex]):focus-visible` (--bd-rule-w2, offset --bd-s1 = 4px, --bd-accent). examples/hirelane/components/board/shell/Foot.tsx:86-87 renders `<details className="bd-register"><summary>`, styled as the twin of `.bd-back` (components/board/style/chrome/the-foot.css:40-62). Tabbing Back -> register shows the accent ring on one twin and the UA's default ring on the other. The two rules also disagree with each other on offset (2px vs 4px), which is what the kit's toast Undo button, mounted outside `.bd-root`, shows. Fixed: add `summary` to both lists (one of them is in hirelane-board-ui's paths), and align the app rule's offset with the room's.

## Flow
- keyboard: Tab to the foot's Back control -> 2px accent ring at 4px offset
- Tab to the register summary beside it -> the browser's default focus ring (no rule matches `summary`)
- fix: `summary` in both selector lists; globals.css offset to the room's step; a test that derives the tag list from the JSX

## Expected impact
Keyboard users see one focus ring on every control in the foot instead of two styles on twin controls. Could break: nothing functional; a ring appears where the UA's was.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one focus ring across sibling controls
Before: 1 of the foot's 2 twin controls (summary) matched by neither focus rule; 2 rules with different offsets
After: 0 unmatched; 1 offset (predicted)
Method: simulation - read from the CSS and the JSX; the fix's main site (the-room.css) is outside this round's paths and the ring needs a browser to see
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Hirelane declares six runtime dependencies nothing in the app imports
evidence:
$ git grep -lE "from ['\"](three|@react-three|openai|clsx|lucide-react)" -- examples/hirelane  -> (nothing)
examples/hirelane/package.json: "openai": "7.10.0", "three": "0.184.0", "@react-three/fiber": "9.6.1", "@react-three/drei": "10.7.7", "clsx": "2.1.1", "lucide-react": "1.41.0", dev "@types/three"
examples/demo-kit/package.json:35 "clsx": "2.1.1" (the kit declares its own)
body:
## Summary
examples/hirelane/package.json declares openai, three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, clsx and lucide-react (and @types/three) with zero importers in the app; they are left from the reviewed-out directions and the removed CopilotKit chat.

## Description
`git grep -E "from ['\"](openai|three|@react-three|clsx|lucide-react)"` over examples/hirelane (app, components, lib, design, test) finds nothing; the only mentions are prose in DESIGN-LAW.md and the reviewed-out briefs, and components/board/marks/Marks.tsx:3 and design/board-brief.md:116 say lucide-react is not used. The kit hirelane transpiles (examples/demo-kit) imports only clsx of these, and declares clsx itself (examples/demo-kit/package.json:35). The app/providers.tsx header records that CopilotKit, the only reason for an openai client, is gone. Each unused entry is install weight, audit surface and lockfile churn for a demo app, and three plus react-three is the largest set in the tree. Fixed: drop the seven entries and regenerate the lockfile. Out of this round's paths: package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml are not in the context map's file list for hirelane-app-and-tests.

## Flow
- git grep the import specifiers across examples/hirelane -> 0 importers for 6 runtime deps
- remove them from package.json, pnpm install, run the three gates and next build
- add a dependency-has-importer test so the list cannot regrow unread

## Expected impact
A smaller install and audit surface for the app, measured by the declared-dependency count (11 runtime -> 5). Could break: a dynamic import or a transitive peer the grep cannot see; next build is the check.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the app declares only what it imports
Before: 6 of 11 runtime dependencies (plus @types/three) with zero importers, by grep
After: 0 of 5 (predicted)
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep on the real tree; removal needs a lockfile write outside this round's paths and a next build
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The one route has no error state: a failed board read shows Next's default page
evidence:
$ ls examples/hirelane/app -> actions.ts globals.css layout.tsx page.tsx providers.tsx
examples/hirelane/app/page.tsx:19 return <Board board={buildBoard()} />;
body:
## Summary
examples/hirelane/app/page.tsx renders `buildBoard()` in a server component with no `app/error.tsx` beside it, so a database that cannot be opened or read paints the framework's generic error screen rather than the board's own words.

## Description
examples/hirelane/app/page.tsx:19 `return <Board board={buildBoard()} />` reads SQLite synchronously (lib/db.ts opens `data/hirelane.sqlite` under cwd). There is no app/error.tsx, app/global-error.tsx or app/loading.tsx (`ls examples/hirelane/app` lists actions.ts, globals.css, layout.tsx, page.tsx, providers.tsx). A locked or corrupt file, or an unwritable data directory, throws during render and the user gets Next's default error page in the board's dark room's absence: no ground colour, no type, no way back but reload. The state-coverage question 'what shows when it FAILS' has no designed answer. Fixed: an app/error.tsx in the direction's tokens that says the pipeline could not be read and offers retry (reset()). Lane C because the surface is new UI whose look has to be judged in a browser, and the app has one route by design (test/nav.test.ts), so a reviewer should confirm an error boundary is wanted in the demo.

## Flow
- make data/hirelane.sqlite unreadable (or lock it) -> load / -> buildBoard throws in the server component
- Next renders its default error page; nothing in the app's voice says what failed
- fix: app/error.tsx (client component) using --bd-* tokens, a sentence naming the store, and reset()

## Expected impact
A demo that hits a bad store fails in its own words with a retry, instead of a framework page. Could break: nothing on the happy path; an error.tsx only renders on a throw.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the route's failure state is designed
Before: 0 of 3 data-source states (zero rows, failure, never returns) beyond the happy path have a designed surface on /
After: failure designed (1 of 3); zero rows is impossible from the seed
Method: simulation - read the route tree; rendering the failure needs a browser and a broken store
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
